Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection, reporting neck pain and stiffness that began
shortly after the event. The reported symptoms are consistent with the mechanism and force of the crash. Over the
course of fifteen visits, care consisted of conservative management including manual therapy, passive
range-of-motion exercises, and a home stretching program, which followed a typical progression for cervical strain.
Examination revealed paraspinal muscle tenderness and reduced cervical range of motion that support the diagnosis,
while neurological screening and several other tests were within normal limits. No prior injury or treatment to the
cervical region is known to this provider. Symptoms improved steadily, and visit frequency was reduced accordingly
as functional status recovered. Billing records reflect single charges for each service rendered, with no duplicate or
repeated entries. Patient was discharged to self-directed home exercise with instructions to return if symptoms recur.
</page>
